title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Early Diagnosis of Potentially Malignant Skin Lesions: A Cross-Sectional Study in a Population Assisted by the Public Health System in Brazil
content: Abstract: This study aims to evaluate the impact of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm developed for diagnosing potentially malignant skin lesions in shortening the time between diagnosis and treatment in a population assisted by the public health system in a Brazilian municipality. This study included 492 patients with dermatological lesions. Images of skin lesions were processed by an AI algorithm and classified as benign or atypical/malignant. Two dermatologists evaluated the same lesions to determine the agreement rate with the AI diagnosis. The time between the primary care consultation and the specialist evaluation, and the time between the diagnosis by the dermatologist and the biopsy of the atypical/malignant lesions were estimated. There was substantial agreement between dermatologists, and reasonable but significant agreement between the AI algorithm and the dermatologists. The AI model predicted malignant lesions with a sensitivity of 89.2%, specificity of 34.4% and accuracy of 78.8%. The mean time between the primary care consultation and the specialist evaluation was 188 ± 96 days, and between the specialist diagnosis and the biopsy of the atypical/malignant lesions was 25 ± 10 days. In conclusion, there was reasonable agreement between the AI algorithm and dermatologists. AI-powered support tools could empower primary care physicians to deliver faster and more precise diagnoses, expedite referrals for suspected malignant skin lesions, and reduce delays in treatment.
